questions.text: What makes a comparison a controlled ablation of connector architecture in a VLM?

options.A: Changing the connector and training data while retaining the model name.
options.B: Comparing two published checkpoints using their best reported scores.
options.C: Changing the connector while holding the other experimental settings fixed.
options.D: Changing the encoder and resolution while retaining the connector.

questions.explanation: A controlled ablation varies the axis being tested and holds other settings fixed, including data, backbone, token budget, and evaluation.

questions.text: You want to test whether denser captions improve your VLM. Which experiment best isolates caption quality?

options.A: Keep images, backbone, connector, resolution, and training budget fixed; vary captions.
options.B: Replace both captions and the vision encoder, then compare final scores.
options.C: Compare a small short-caption model with a much larger dense-caption model.
options.D: Increase image resolution only for the dense-caption training run.

questions.explanation: Holding the other axes and training budget fixed makes caption quality the experimental variable instead of confounding it with model or compute changes.

questions.text: The picker filters candidates with r.llm_b <= budget_b. A recipe has llm_b=7, but its vision encoder and connector bring the total above 8B. With budget_b=8, what happens?

options.A: It is rejected because the filter sums all component parameter counts.
options.B: It remains eligible because the filter checks only the LLM parameter count.
options.C: Its encoder and connector are removed to fit the total parameter budget.
options.D: It raises ValueError because the total parameter count exceeds the budget.

questions.explanation: The filter reads only llm_b. It does not calculate total model size, memory requirements, or latency.
